Creating a Terraform Provider for Just About Anything
创建一个几乎适用于任何事物的Terraform提供商

Published 8:00 AM UTC Dec 19, 2018 发表于2018年12月19日 UTC 上午8：00

Learn how to contribute to a Terraform provider or create your own from this walkthrough.
了解如何为Terraform供应商贡献资源，或从本攻略中创建自己的服务。

If you are looking to create a new Terraform provider, this HashiCorp Learn Tutorial will help you get started. 如果你想创建一个新的Terraform服务提供商，这份HashiCorp学习教程将帮助你入门。

Terrafom is an amazing tool that lets you define your infrastructure as code. Under the hood it's an incredibly powerful state machine that makes API requests and marshals resources.
Terrafom 是一个很棒的工具，可以让你用代码定义基础设施。它的核心是一个极其强大的状态机，负责发送API请求并管理资源。

In this talk, Eddie Zaneski, manager of developer relations at DigitalOcean, will dive into the inner workings of Terraform and examine all the elements of a provider—from the documentation to the test suite. You'll walk away with the knowledge of how to contribute to an existing provider or create your own from scratch.
在本次演讲中，DigitalOcean开发者关系经理Eddie Zaneski将深入探讨Terraform的内部运作，并分析供应商的所有要素——从文档到测试套件。你将获得如何为现有服务提供者贡献资金或从零开始创建自己的服务的知识离开。

Zaneski will also take a look at some of the things he encountered while working on the DigitalOcean provider and the lessons learned from the community.
Zaneski还将回顾他在DigitalOcean服务商工作中遇到的一些问题，以及从社区中获得的经验教训。

Speakers
演讲者

  • Eddie Zaneski 埃迪·扎内斯基Manager of Developer Relations, DigitalOcean, Digital Ocean 开发者关系经理，DigitalOcean，Digital Ocean

How's it going, everyone? My name is Eddie Zaneski and I serve the developer community at a company called Digital Ocean. Quick show of hands here, who has used a Digital Ocean tutorial before? That's a lot of people. Despite what many people think, we are not a tutorial company, we are a cloud provider, So we've got all those things that you need to do cool stuff.
大家好吗？我叫Eddie Zaneski，在一家名为Digital Ocean的公司服务开发者社区。这里快速举手，谁用过Digital Ocean的教程？那是很多人。尽管很多人认为我们不是教程公司，我们是一家云服务商，所以我们拥有你做酷炫事情所需的所有功能。

Today we're here to talk about Terraform. I'm also joined by a few awesome colleagues from DO, especially Tom right over there. Wave your hand, Tom. We have a huge Enterprise Vault deployment internally, so if you want to talk about roll-your-own Vault deployment, come see Tom at our booth over there.
今天我们要来谈谈Terraform。我还有几位来自DO的优秀同事，尤其是那边的Tom。挥挥手，汤姆。我们内部有一个庞大的企业保险库部署，如果你想谈谈自组部署，欢迎来我们那边的展位找Tom。

What is Terraform?
什么是Terraform？

What is Terraform? Can I get a gauge of the audience, who here has used Terraform? Hands up. That's most of everyone. Who here has contributed to, or written a Terraform provider? We don't need to talk too much about what Terraform is, we do need to talk about how Elon Musk wants to terraform Mars, but all right.
什么是Terraform？能给我一个用户群的概率吗？这里有谁用过Terraform？举起手来。大多数人都是这样。这里有谁参与过或编写过Terraform的服务？我们不需要多谈什么是地球化，我们确实需要谈谈埃隆·马斯克想改造火星，好吧。

I like to describe Terraform as a giant state machine. We can talk about "It's infrastructure as code," we can talk about a lot of things, but at end of the day, Terraform is a great state machine. There's that little terraform.state file that you see, and the nice thing is that you can have any resource that is backed by some form of an API. It can be a JSON API, gRPC, XML API, any type of resource that is backed by an API can be turned into a Terraform provider.
我喜欢把Terraform描述为一个巨大的状态机器。我们可以谈论“基础设施即代码”，可以讨论很多话题，但归根结底，Terraform 是一个很棒的状态机。你看到的那个小 terraform.state 文件，好处是你可以拥有任何由某种 API 支持的资源。它可以是JSON API、gRPC、XML API，任何由API支持的资源都可以转化为Terraform提供者。

What Terraform does at its heart is really just marshaling resources between a JSON payload and an internal Terraform struct called a resource, we'll talk about. As awesome as this tool is, its roots are simple and it's not that complicated to pick up. Terraform is a state machine, what is a Terraform provider? Like I said, any resource that is backed by an API can be turned into a Terraform provider.
Terraform 的核心其实就是在 JSON 负载和内部的 Terraform 结构体（称为资源）之间进行资源的汇集，我们稍后会详细说明。这个工具虽然很棒，但它的根源很简单，上手也不算复杂。Terraform 是一个状态机，什么是 Terraform 提供者？正如我说的，任何有API支持的资源都可以转化为Terraform的提供者。

Examples of Terraform providers
Terraform 提供者示例

There are something like 90 Terraform providers that are supported. Here's a quick example. You have a provider and then you have this attribute in there for a token and then a resource. You've all seen HCL before. You can manage resources, you can manage your servers. You can also manage things like Kubernetes. with a Terraform provider for Kubernetes. Instead of writing all of that giant Kubernetes YAML, you can now define your Kubernetes services in HCL, which is a lot better. There's not a ton of repeat, there's not a ton of nesting.
大约有90个Terraform供应商被支持。这里有一个简短的例子。你有一个提供者，然后你有一个属性，代表一个令牌，然后是一个资源。你们都见过HCL。你可以管理资源，也可以管理服务器。你也可以管理像Kubernetes这样的设备。为 Kubernetes 提供了 Terraform 服务。你不必再编写那些庞大的KubernetesYAML代码，现在可以用HCL定义Kubernetes服务，这要好得多。重复不多，筑巢也不多。

Has anyone done this yet? Has anyone used HCL with Kubernetes? Have you liked the experience? That's a thumbs-up. Not only can we do things infrastructure and service related, there's the GitHub provider that everyone's probably seen and the cool thing about this is that it's an API. We have a provider for it, so we can manage this resource via Terraform state. Can you imagine on your first day of work, you come in for engineering onboarding, and all you have to do is make a pull request to this single repo to get access to everything you want.
有人做过这个吗？有人用过 HCL 配合 Kubernetes 吗？你喜欢这次经历吗？这是个赞。我们不仅能做基础设施和服务相关的工作，还有大家可能都见过的GitHub提供商，而且它的酷炫之处在于它是一个API。我们有供应商，所以可以通过Terraform state管理这个资源。你能想象第一天上班时，你来做工程入职培训，只需对这个单一仓库发起拉取请求，就能访问你想要的所有资源。

You can define your users in here, you can define your repos. Instead of having to hunt down that one person on your DevOps team who can create GitHub repos, you can just make a PR to your GitHub's repos repo, and it's just a giant Terraform file. Then you can add it, add all the users that are already in there as data sources and pull them in and grant access that way, create teams that way. You can start to see where we're going with this.
你可以在这里定义你的用户，也可以定义你的仓库。与其去找你DevOps团队里那个能创建GitHub仓库的人，你只需对GitHub仓库创建一个PR，它就是一个巨大的Terraform文件。然后你可以添加它，把已经存在的所有用户作为数据源，把他们拉进来并授权访问权限，这样创建团队。你应该能明白我们要说什么了。

Then we can do something like the marvelous Seth Vargo has done, where he created a Terraform provider for Google Calendar. What if we took all of our Google Calendar events and represented them in some kind of Terraform state? He wrote an awesome blog post that y'all should check out. It worked really well.
然后我们可以做一些像塞斯·瓦尔戈那样的事，他为谷歌日历创建了一个Terraform服务。如果我们把所有谷歌日历事件都用某种Terraform状态表示，会怎样？他写了一篇很棒的博客文章，你们一定要看看。效果非常好。

What other things can we play with? What other types of providers can we make? Who here has heard of the Philips Hue light bulbs? I wrote a Terraform provider for the Philips Hue light bulbs. We use the attributes at the top to find the bridge that it's going to talk to and then we pull in a data resource. Who here has used data resources? Do I need to explain them?
我们还能玩玩什么？我们还能制造哪些其他类型的服务提供者？这里有谁听说过飞利浦Hue灯泡？我为飞利浦Hue灯泡编写了一份Terraform供应商。我们用顶部的属性来找到它要通信的桥接节点，然后拉入数据资源。这里有谁用过数据资源？我需要解释吗？

With data resources, you have a resource that is being created and it's mutable, you're messing around with it. A data resource would be something that you don't want to modify but you want to import as read-only. There's an import command, where you can import a resource but then when you run terraform destroy, that resource gets destroyed. A data resource is just like a permanent read-only thing.
对于数据资源，你有一个正在创建且可变的资源，你只是随意调整它。数据资源是你不想修改，但想导入为只读的资源。有一个导入命令，你可以导入资源，但当你运行 terraform destroy 时，那个资源会被摧毁。数据资源就像一个永久只读的东西。

I pull in the light_id of my kitchen and then I set the color to some kind of awesome fuchsia and boom. Now we're managing an actual resource in the real world with Terraform. What if we also did something like managing our to-do lists? I created another Terraform provider, this one's on GitHub. I used a to-do list client called Todoist, it's got an API behind it. What if we implement these things so we can see them in the real world?
我把厨房light_id拉进来，然后把颜色调成一种很棒的紫红色，砰。现在我们用Terraform管理现实世界的资源。如果我们还做点什么，比如管理待办事项清单呢？我创建了另一个 Terraform 提供商，这个在 GitHub 上。我用过一个叫Todoist的待办事项客户端，它背后有API。如果我们把这些东西实现出来，让我们能在现实世界中看到它们呢？

I have a quick demo that I'll show you of this Terraform provider. We'll start with that main.tf file and we'll pull in the provider and then you pass it an API key but it's configured to an environment variable so you can't hack me. Then we got a resource we'll call this todoist_task and I'll call this talk. Then we can have some content: "Give talk", boom. We save that: terraform init, terraform apply. It wants to create a resource, boom. If I pop over to my to-do list, we can see that it's created a resource. We can go in there, and we can say, "Give talk right now" and update it, and it will update the content. You get where this is going.
我有一个简短的演示，可以给你看这个Terraform供应商。我们会从那个 main.tf 文件开始，拉入提供者，然后你传递一个API密钥，但它被设置为环境变量，所以你无法入侵我。然后我们有了资源，称之为todoist_task，我称之为演讲。然后我们就能有一些内容：“演讲”，砰。我们保存它：Terraform init，Terraform 应用。它想创造资源，砰。如果我打开待办事项列表，可以看到它创建了一个资源。我们可以进去，说“现在就来演讲”并更新内容，它也会更新内容。你明白我的意思。

We can do things like mark it as completed. "Completed" equals "true," and we save that, and it's gonna disappear 'cause it was marked as completed. Let's bring it back, and then we can do something like, the data resource I was talking about, so we'll have data, todoist_project, so I can categorize these as projects. I'll call this my talks project, and then the name of it will be "talks." I'm going to show you how this is working, it's not just showing it off.
我们可以做一些事情，比如标记为已完成。“完成”等于“真”，我们保存它，它会消失，因为它被标记为已完成。我们把它拉回来，然后我们可以做类似我说的数据资源，这样我们就有数据，todoist_project，这样我可以把它们分类为项目。我称它为我的讲座项目，然后它的名字就是“讲座”。我会给你展示这个方法的运作方式，不仅仅是展示。

Then we have a project_id. We'll do some interpolation, so data.todoist_project.talks.id. Save that. It's mad about something, of course. Oh, it's 'cause it's already created. So terraform destroy. The API's a little wonky, can't change your project once it's created. Created, boom. If we look down here, "Talks" popped up there.
然后我们就有project_id。我们会做一些插值，所以data.todoist_project.talks.id。省省吧。当然，它在疯狂。哦，是因为它已经被创造出来了。所以地球改造，摧毁。API有点不稳定，项目创建后无法更改。一声创造，砰。如果我们往下看，“Talks”这个名字就出现在那儿。

We took a resource that already existed, which was our project, pulled it in as a data resource so we could reference that in another resource. That's the power of Terraform. Let's dive into how that works.
我们拿了一个已经存在的资源，也就是我们的项目，把它作为数据资源拉入，以便可以在另一个资源中引用它。这就是Terraform的力量。让我们深入探讨一下这是如何运作的。

Why would we want to create Terraform providers?
我们为什么要创建Terraform供应商？

Why would we want to create these Terraform providers? Can I get a show of hands, who here has made a Terraform provider? That's a few of you. How many of you have made one for internal stuff? Just about the same amount of people, a few less.
我们为什么要创建这些Terraform供应商？请大家举个手，这里有谁做过Terraform服务商？这就是你们中的几个人。你们中有多少人为内部工作做过一个？人数差不多，只是少了几位。

Some of the things you might want to build a provider for: Maybe you're a cloud provider and you want to have a Terraform provider for your customers to use. Maybe your customers have asked for one, so they can manage your resources inside HCL and Terraform. You have a resource in an API that makes sense to manage with Terraform. Some nice things to do with this, you can skip a frontend entirely. If you're working with HCL in Terraform configuration files, you don't need someone to write that React frontend. You also don't need to create little duct tape apps that implement the API that you have. Everyone's had to do a little one-off app that they run and it does all the magic.
你可能需要构建服务提供商的一些方面：也许你是云服务提供商，想为客户提供一个Terraform提供商。也许你的客户已经要求了，这样他们就能在HCL和Terraform中管理你的资源。你有一个资源，API里的资源可以用Terraform管理。这里有一些不错的做法，你可以完全跳过前端。如果你在 Terraform 配置文件中使用 HCL，你不需要别人写那个 React 前端。你也不需要创建那些实现你现有API的小胶带应用。每个人都得自己做一个小型的一次性应用，它就能实现所有的神奇功能。

With Terraform you don't need to do that because Terraform is acting as your frontend API client. The next reason is internal. Building internal providers for Terraform is where I really see the power here. We have a Terraform provider called terraform-provider-dointernal. This is a very shallow shim/fork of our public one and it adds a few additional fields to it. If Terraform providers are written in Go, they're simple Go plugins. They're binaries that get compiled and spin up a little RPC server that talks to the main Terraform process. It's really cool under the hood, so I have some resources at the end so you can read about them.
用 Terraform 你不需要这么做，因为它是你的前端 API 客户端。下一个原因是内心的。我真正看到的就是为Terraform构建内部服务商。我们有一个叫 terraform-provider-dointernal 的 Terraform 服务商。这是我们公共接口的一个非常浅的垫片/分支，并且增加了几个额外的字段。如果 Terraform 提供者是用 Go 编写的，它们就是简单的 Go 插件。它们是二进制文件，被编译后启动一个小型RPC服务器，与主Terraform进程通信。它内部真的很酷，所以我在最后附了一些资源，你可以去了解。

But the way this actually works is, we have an internal repo that we can pull in the public repo and with Go, you can just add a file with the same package name and compile it and everything magically gets compiled. You don't need to do some crazy overwriting, Go will just compile everything with the same package name.
但实际上，我们有一个内部仓库，可以在公开仓库里拉取它，用 Go 时，你只需添加一个同包名的文件并编译，所有东西就会神奇地被编译完成。你不需要做什么疯狂的覆盖，Go 会用相同的包名编译所有东西。

We have a few additional fields that are represented, like hypervisor placement. This can influence where our VMs get placed physically through our server racks. You want to register into the Chef server, for internal management droplets. We can also expose some beta features to internal people because our teams in DO are using Terraform to manage some of our infrastructure.
我们还有几个额外的字段，比如虚拟机监控器放置。这会影响虚拟机在服务器机架中的物理位置。你需要注册到 Chef 服务器，以便内部管理 droplet。我们也可以向内部人员展示一些测试版功能，因为我们DO团队正在使用Terraform管理部分基础设施。

I was talking with someone I met last night who works at Target and they have some big beefy F5 load balancers. If anyone's ever worked with F5 load balancers, you know that you define your rules via ASIC firmware. You have to go in, you have to write a bunch of ASIC firmware, compile that and you flash your load balancers so they have your rules.
我昨晚和一个在Target工作的人聊过，他们有一些大而强劲的F5负载均衡器。如果有人用过F5负载均衡器，你就知道规则是通过ASIC固件定义的。你得自己写一堆ASIC固件，编译出来，然后刷入负载均衡器，让它们有你的规则。

These guys have built an API that handles all of that, so they can go in, make API requests, and that API will compile their firmware and flash it into their F5 load balancers. Now he's interested in building a Terraform provider, because now you can add your rules to your HCL and you don't have to have whatever frontend you were using before. You don't have to have your curl request, you don't have to use Postman. Hopefully some of the wheels are starting to turn, and you're thinking of some internal APIs that you can build a provider for.
这些人构建了一个 API 来处理所有这些，这样他们就可以进去发 API 请求，这个 API 会编译他们的固件并刷入他们的 F5 负载均衡器。现在他有兴趣构建一个Terraform提供商，因为现在你可以把规则添加到HCL，不用再用之前用的前端了。你不必提出卷发请求，也不必使用邮递员。希望现在已经开始运转，你也在考虑一些内部API可以构建一个供应商。

A couple people here have contributed to a provider. You might want to contribute so you can fix a bug, add a feature that's missing. Quick plug for Hacktoberfest: It's a thing we're running with GitHub and Twilio. If you've made 5 pull requests during the month of October, we'll send you a sweet T-shirt, so check it out.
这里有几个人曾向某个服务提供者做出过贡献。你可能想贡献一些，这样你就能修复一个漏洞，添加缺失的功能。快速推荐一下Hacktoberfest：这是我们和GitHub、Twilio一起运营的活动。如果你在十月份内提交了5个拉取请求，我们会送你一件精美的T恤，敬请关注。

You might also want to maintain a fork of a provider that exists, so we maintained a fork of the Cloudflare provider, because there were some enterprise features that weren't implemented yet. We have a legacy account, so we have some different older policies that aren't supported via the new API. If there is a provider that you need to make some changes on you can fork it and just manage it yourself.
你可能还想维护一个已存在的供应商分支，所以我们维护了Cloudflare供应商的一个分支，因为有些企业功能尚未实现。我们有一个遗留账户，所以有些旧策略不支持，新API不支持。如果有供应商需要修改，你可以分叉自己管理。

With Terraform, everything is convention first
而Terraform则是先遵循约定

The important thing to understand when it comes to working with Terraform is, everything is convention first. I learned Go through working on Terraform and lots of people have told me that was a very big mistake, because originally Terraform was written by some Ruby developers and they're definitely great at Go now. Fun fact, the original Terraform code was written inside of the Digital Ocean office by Mitchell [Hashimoto] because he was in New York for the summer and it was really hot and they wanted to come to Digital Ocean's air-conditioned office. Everything was done through convention. This is something that you have to accept. If you're a hardcore Go developer and you're going to see some of the functions and you're going to see some underscores in there with some snake casing you're going to be a little cringy. You just have to embrace that convention comes first.
使用Terraform时，重要的是要明白，一切都首先遵循约定。我是通过开发Terraform学会Go的，很多人告诉我这是个很大的错误，因为最初Terraform是由一些Ruby开发者编写的，他们现在的Go技术确实很棒。有趣的是，最初的Terraform代码是由Mitchell（桥本）在Digital Ocean办公室里写的，因为他夏天在纽约，天气很热，他们想来Digital Ocean的空调办公室。一切都是按照惯例进行的。这是你必须接受的事情。如果你是核心Go开发者，看到一些功能和底线和蛇形外壳，你可能会觉得有点尴尬。你只需要接受传统优先。

Where should you start?
你应该从哪里开始？

Where you need to start is with a Go API client. For that Todoist provider I showed you I had to build a Go API client. You should look at it. It's definitely not well written because I don't know Go that well. But this is where you start, you need to have a strong API client, because the important thing is to separate your API's logic from your Terraform provider's logic. If there is any type of weirdness in your API, you want to address that in the API client. You don't want to have to put shims and duct tape in your provider. You want to abstract these things as much as possible. Your client needs to have superb error handling, 'cause we're going to talk about what to do when shit breaks. You should have some kind of logging mechanism so you can quickly identify when something is broken if it's related to Terraform or your API or your client. Start with a strong API client.
你需要从Go API客户端开始。对于我之前给你展示的那个Todoist供应商，我必须构建一个 Go API 客户端。你应该看看。这肯定写得不好，因为我对Go不太了解。但这才是起点，你需要一个强大的API客户端，因为重要的是把你的API逻辑和Terraform提供者的逻辑分开。如果你的 API 有任何异常，你需要在 API 客户端中解决。你不想在供应商里装垫片和胶带。你要尽可能抽象这些东西。你的客户需要有出色的错误处理能力，因为我们会讨论当事情出现问题时该怎么办。你应该有某种日志机制，这样你能快速识别出问题，无论是与Terraform、API还是客户端有关。从一个强大的API客户端开始。

Skeletons/guides available for getting started
有适合入门的骨架/指南

There are skeletons available for starting with the provider. This guide down here is the most important resource to read so check that out for getting started. Schema is the most important thing to understand
模式是理解最重要的东西

Schema is the most important this to understand here. This comes after that line of the Func declaration. You return a Schema.Provider. Everything in here is done through resource maps. You have maps of a property name to a Schema declaration. In that Todoist provider, remember I said you had to clear the API key if it wasn't through an environment variable. This is what that looks like, you have this tiny little Schema and Terraform immediately knows how to take the variable and assign where it needs to go. It works magically under the hood. The important thing to note is that all the type enforcement for Terraform is done in the Schema, so while you're developing your plug-in and your Go functions and your CRUD functions, you need to trust... This is where the Go developers are gonna say, "Ugh!" You need to trust that the data coming in is what you declared it is in the Schema. You're hesitant at first, but the Schema level, the external, it won't slurp up that HDL file successfully if the Schema is wrong, so you have to trust that everything coming in is mapped to the Schema correctly. Or else you're gonna have a lot of garbage code.
这里最重要的是理解模式。这句话紧随Func宣言的那句之后。你返回一个Schema.Provider。这里的所有操作都是通过资源地图完成的。你有属性名称到模式声明的映射。在那个 Todoist 提供者里，记得我说过如果 API 密钥不是通过环境变量，就必须清除。这就是它的样子，你有一个很小的模式，Terraform 立刻知道如何拿这个变量并分配它需要去的地方。它在引擎盖下神奇地运作着。重要的是要注意，Terraform 的所有类型强制执行都在 Schema 中完成，所以在开发插件、Go 功能和 CRUD 函数时，你需要信任......这时候，Go的开发者们肯定会说：“呃！”你需要相信输入的数据是你在Schema中声明的那样。你一开始会犹豫，但Schema层级，外部文件，如果Schema错了，它就无法成功接收HDL文件，所以你必须相信所有输入的数据都正确映射到Schema。否则你会有很多垃圾代码。

Error handling
错误处理

Error handling. This is extremely important. Going back to the API client, you need to make sure that your API logic is separated from your Terraform provider logic. If there are Band-Aids you need to put in place, fix your API, fix your client, try not to have this in your provider. For your provider to be successful and to be easy to use, you need to have extremely robust error handling and it needs to be fault tolerant. You need to handle that random Cloudflare 506 that you get back which is an HTML page for some reason from a JSON response. You need to have logic to handle that. You don't have to handle that specific case, but you need to have some error method that knows how this gets handled.
错误处理。这非常重要。回到 API 客户端，你需要确保你的 API 逻辑和 Terraform 提供者逻辑是分开的。如果需要临时措施，就修正你的API，修复你的客户端，尽量不要在你的提供商里设置这些。为了让你的服务商成功且易于使用，你需要拥有极其强大的错误处理能力，并且具备容错能力。你需要处理那个随机的Cloudflare 506文件，它不知为何是JSON响应的一个HTML页面。你需要有逻辑来应对这种情况。你不必处理那个具体情况，但你需要有某种错误方法来处理这个过程。

You want to make sure you log all the things. There's a great functionality built into the helpers for logging. You can just TF_LOG=INFO, debug, different log levels and it will print out a bunch of stuff, so you're going to use this a lot as you're building your providers. Coming back, you need to quickly identify what's your API's fault versus what's Terraform's fault versus what's random. If we look at this little stack trace here, This is from the Terraform docs, you're going to see this type of thing a lot, which is a giant panic stack trace when something goes wrong.
你要确保所有事情都记录下来。辅助工具内置了一个很棒的功能用于日志记录。你只需TF_LOG=INFO、调试、不同的日志层级，它就能打印出很多内容，所以你在构建提供者时会经常用到这些。回到现在，你需要快速区分哪些是你的 API 的问题，哪些是 Terraform 的问题，哪些是随机的。如果我们看看这里的这个小栈轨迹，这是来自 Terraform 文档，你会经常看到这种东西，这是一个巨大的恐慌栈轨迹，当出现问题时。

They tell you the key part of this message is the first two lines, so just note here, you want to identify what is your responsibility as quickly as you can, just like reading any stack trace, and they jump right into the actual resource file in the line.
他们告诉你这条消息的关键部分是前两行，所以这里要注意，你要尽快确定你的责任，就像读取任何栈跟踪一样，他们会直接跳到该行的实际资源文件。

You'll see these stack traces a lot. Quickly identify what's your fault. Partial state is another thing that you'll have to deal with, and so this is where maybe your resource was created or updated, but only part of it was. Maybe the error happened after part of the resource got updated, and so there's a quick call-out from the docs here: "If the Create callback returns with or without an error and an ID has been set, the resource is assumed created and all state is saved with it."
你会经常看到这些堆栈痕迹。迅速找出你的错。部分状态也是你必须处理的，所以也许你的资源就是在这里被创建或更新的，但实际上只有部分内容。也许错误发生在部分资源更新之后，所以文档里有个简短说明：“如果创建回调返回时有无错误且已设置ID，资源被假定已创建，所有状态随之保存。”

That is very important. Read through this page at the bottom here. They have a very large declaration on what happens to handle these errors. Just to make sure we understand, if you look at the very bottom there. That SetId function. As long as that is successful, and as long as an ID is set, no matter what other errors are happening, it's going to assume that your resource was created successfully. A lot of caveats to learn, so read the docs at the bottom there and build extreme, well-done error handling in.
这非常重要。请阅读底部的这一页。他们有一份非常详细的声明来处理这些错误。为了确认我们理解，如果你看最底下。那个 SetId 函数。只要成功，只要设置了 ID，无论还发生了什么错误，它都会假设你的资源是成功创建的。有很多注意事项要学，所以请阅读底部的文档，并构建出极致且出色的错误处理方法。

Testing
测试

Testing. This is the biggest pain point that I have run into while working on these providers, and it's not that it's not well done. If you think about, "How do you provide a testing framework to test against a real API that's creating real resources in real time?" This is where you're going to spend the most time is understanding these test frameworks, and the test framework is well done. It's just there's a lot here. So walk through it with me real quick. This resource.Test function is how we declare a test. It takes in a resource test case. It has a PreCheck function. This is where you set up your API client and do a bunch of other stuff. You declare your providers. These are usually defined in one shared function. In one test config file, and then you declare a check destroy function, and so after all your steps will run Terraform.
测试。这是我在处理这些服务商时遇到的最大痛点，并不是说做得不好。如果你想想，“如何提供一个测试框架，用来测试一个实时创造真实资源的真实 API？”你花最多时间去理解这些测试框架，而测试框架做得很好。只是这里的东西太多了。那就跟我快速讲一遍吧。这个资源。测试函数是我们宣告测试的方式。它会接收资源测试用例。它有预检功能。这里是你设置API客户端和做一堆其他事情的地方。你申报你的服务提供者。这些通常定义在一个共享函数中。在一个测试配置文件里，然后你声明一个检查销毁函数，所以所有步骤后你都会运行Terraform。

Terraform will basically run terraform apply on your test case. It will run through all of your test steps to make sure things are done, and then it will make sure that all of your resources are done, so you provided a function to assert that your resources are actually destroyed. The resource test steps here, this is the bread and butter of the testing, so every test step has a Terraform config. So you can see here, we want to do reusability, so this is an acceptance test, that's the testAcc, so test acceptance check to do is TaskConfig_basic, so you'll have a lot of different configs. They look like this. You can define a function and it takes in the templated thing, and you use format string to print it, but you're just testing a Terraform config in string form.
Terraform 基本上会在你的测试用例上运行 Terraform 应用。它会运行你所有的测试步骤以确保完成，然后确保你所有的资源都已经完成，所以你提供了一个函数来断言你的资源实际上已经被销毁。这里的资源测试步骤，是测试的核心，所以每个测试步骤都有 Terraform 配置。你可以看到这里，我们想要实现可复用性，所以这是一个验收测试，也就是 testAcc，所以要做的验收检查是TaskConfig_basic的，所以你会有很多不同的配置。它们长这样。你可以定义一个函数，它会接收模板化的内容，然后用格式字符串来打印，但你只是测试字符串形式的 Terraform 配置。

You don't have to declare your provider. That's all done at the start. You take a basic function like this, you plug it into the config for the test step, and then it has a bunch of helper methods that can do something like resource that, check resource attribute and it knows how to check that Todoist task test, the content matches whatever content you expect it to. You're spinning up resources, asserting that they got defined where they are, and then moving onto the next step, and so you can have many tests for a single config, and you use these steps to simulate things like updates and modifies.
你不必申报你的服务提供者。这些都是在开始时完成的。你拿一个基本函数，把它插入测试步骤的配置里，然后它会有一堆辅助方法，比如资源处理，检查资源属性，它知道如何检查Todoist任务测试，内容是否符合你预期的内容。你是在启动资源，声明它们已经定义好，然后进入下一步，这样你可以对单个配置进行多次测试，并用这些步骤模拟更新和修改等操作。

HashiCorp has a TeamCity server, which is JetBrains' CI/CD server, and so all of their providers are continuously tested. One of the requirements to be an official provider is you have to provide them with the actual API key that they can use to test a provider. This is constantly spinning up resources, asserting that everything is working, and that they're assuring the quality of these providers.
HashiCorp 有一个 TeamCity 服务器，是 JetBrains 的 CI/CD 服务器，因此他们所有的服务提供者都会持续接受测试。成为官方提供者的一个要求是，你必须提供他们实际的API密钥，以便他们用来测试提供者。这不断地启动资源，宣称一切都在正常运行，并且他们保证了这些服务提供者的质量。

Test flow: It starts with that precheck, then it goes through the test steps, then the destroy, then check destroy. You take one config per step, use steps to simulate updates and deletes. Reuse as much as possible while you're writing these early on. It's very easy to get a bunch of spaghetti helpers, a ton of repeated code, so just approach this with the mindset of, "I need to be reusable. I need to be composable." Abstract as much as you can into these tiny functions that you can work with easier.
测试流程：从预检开始，然后经过测试步骤，再是销毁，最后检查销毁。你每步做一个配置，用步骤模拟更新和删除。在早期写这些内容时，尽量重复使用。很容易遇到一堆意大利面帮手，代码重复很多，所以只要抱着“我需要可重复使用”的心态来做这件事。我需要变得可组合。”尽可能抽象到这些你更容易操作的小函数里。

The make file, you definitely want to copy and paste a make file from the skeleton or other providers. Fun fact, we didn't realize that you could run a single acceptance test. We thought you had to run the entire test suite for way too long. You can in fact run a single resource test. So you do like: Make test account, pass the TESTARGS, and the name of the test. It saves you a lot of time, because these test suites can take like... I think ours takes 79 minutes to run, so they run parallel, but a lot of the steps are sequential, because you're modifying resources. The test suite takes a long time. Take advantage of the fact that you can run one test at a time.
关于制作文件，你肯定要从骨架或其他提供者那里复制粘贴制作文件。有趣的是，我们之前没意识到可以做一次验收测试。我们以为整个测试套件运行得太久了。实际上你可以做一次资源测试。所以你会做：创建测试账号，通过TESTARGS，并提供考试名称。这能帮你省很多时间，因为这些测试室可以花......我记得我们的运行需要79分钟，所以它们是并行运行的，但很多步骤是顺序的，因为你是在修改资源。测试套件耗时很长。利用一次只做一个测试的优势。

Docs... It's very easy to get started with these. There is a magic website folder in all the providers, and so we'll look at this real quick. We've got the magic website folder here. This is the index page. So you just have a very simple nav bar with links to the rest of the resources, and then the individual resources are under the docs folder, and then you have the d for data sources, and the r for resources. These are just simple markdown files that you've seen before and are used to working with. It's just a simple markdown file and ERB that's gets parsed out.
医生......这些工具很容易上手。所有服务商中都有一个神奇的网站文件夹，我们会快速看看。我们这里有魔法网站文件夹。这是索引页。所以你只需要一个非常简单的导航栏，链接到其他资源，然后各个资源都在文档文件夹下，然后你有数据源的d和资源的r。这些只是你以前见过、习惯使用的简单Markdown文件。它只是一个简单的markdown文件和ERB被解析出来。

The TeamCity job runs and it takes all of the magic website folders from all the providers, compiles them, and deploys them to the Terraform docs website. They have a really cool CI/CD job that's set up. You don't really have to think about it. If you want to get started contributing to a provider, this is a great place to start, so dive into the docs.
TeamCity 作业运行后，它会从所有供应商那里获取所有 magic 网站文件夹，编译后部署到 Terraform 文档网站。他们有一个非常酷的CI/CD岗位。你其实不用多想。如果你想开始为某家服务提供者捐款，这里是一个很好的起点，所以请深入阅读相关文档。

Process notes
流程说明

Process notes... I think that HashiCorp mentioned this. You want to engage them early. If you are working what you want to be an accepted, not internal, but community provider, engage HashiCorp early. They'll give you the resources. They have a program they'll get you involved in, and they have a Slack for people who are working on providers, so you can get access to other folks who are also building providers. Talk to HashiCorp early. They use Travis CI/CD for GitHub testing. Releases are done via Slack, so this is pretty cool. You pop into that Slack channel and you're like, "Hey! Can someone release version 1.0 of the DigitalOcean Terraform provider?" And then a nice HashiCorp employee comes along. They're like, "Yeah. I got you." There's a lot of magic that happens. They did a really good job structuring out this program to support the 90+ providers they have.
流程笔记......我记得HashiCorp提到过这点。你要尽早让他们参与。如果你想成为一个被接受的、非内部的社区服务提供者，尽早与HashiCorp合作。他们会给你资源。他们有一个项目可以让你参与，还有一个Slack，专门给那些在供应商工作的人，这样你就能接触到其他也在做建筑服务的人。尽早联系HashiCorp。他们用Travis CI/CD做GitHub测试。发布是通过Slack完成的，所以这很酷。你打开那个Slack频道，你会说，“嘿！有人能发布DigitalOcean Terraform提供商的1.0版本吗？”然后，一位和蔼的HashiCorp员工出现了。他们会说，“是的。我抓住你了。”这里发生了很多魔法。他们在支持90+服务提供者的项目结构设计上做得非常好。

The processes at the bottom, if you want to get an accepted, sanctioned provider, go through that. Read it. It's very well done. A couple tips... Learn a bit of Go first. I'm a JavaScript and Ruby developer, so learn Go. You're going to get very familiar with the strconv package. This is going from like ints to strings and strings to ints. You're going to use it a ton, especially because all the IDs in Terraform need to be strings, even if your resource has an integer as an ID, it needs to be a string inside Terraform. You're going to do a ton of converting back and forth and Go will get mad at you if you don't do it right.
如果你想获得一个被认可、认可的医生，就走下面的流程。读一读。做得非常好。几个小建议......先学点“Go”。我是JavaScript和Ruby开发者，所以一定要学Go。你会非常熟悉strconv包。这包括从类似的整数到字符串，再从字符串到整数。你会用到很多，尤其是因为Terraform里的所有ID都需要字符串，即使你的资源ID是整数，也必须是Terraform内部的字符串。你会反复转换很多，如果操作不对，围棋会生你的气。

To get around this you can use custom UnmarshalJSON functions. You can Google it. You can unmarshal into the struct like you're used to, but you declare your own UnmarshalJSON function, and you can have a temporary resource in there that you convert from the ID into the string, and then it's magic, so use those. You'll save a lot of converting on the fly. Have a solid Go API client, fix design problems with your API if possible, understand Terraform modules. We get a bunch of GitHub issues where... There are a few caveats with modules where you need to, even though you're taking a list, you still always need to wrap your lists when you're passing it through a module. Understand how Terraform modules work, because your community and your users are going to take your provider, use it in a module, and then raise issues and bugs about it.
为了绕过这个问题，你可以使用自定义的UnmarshalJSON函数。你可以谷歌一下。你可以像以前那样解封入结构体，但你要声明自己的UnmarshalJSON函数，里面可以有一个临时资源，把ID转换成字符串，然后就很神奇了，所以用这些。你会省去很多临时转换的麻烦。拥有一个稳固的 Go API 客户端，尽可能修复 API 设计上的问题，理解 Terraform 模块。我们会遇到很多GitHub问题......模块有一些需要注意的地方，即使你拿的是列表，传递模块时仍然需要把列表包装。了解Terraform模块的工作原理，因为你的社区和用户会把你的供应商放在模块里，然后提出问题和bug。

HCL 2.0 has null type, which is really great. You can set a resource to null instead of the crazy Go default that's 0 or empty string. Don't be afraid to copy and paste from other providers and your own provider. To add a new resource right now, I just copy from our droplet, which is our server resource provider. Do a find-and-replace everywhere to change the name and then worry about the logic, so copy and paste a ton.
HCL 2.0 有 null 类型，这真的很棒。你可以把资源设置为空，而不是像Go那样疯狂地默认为0或空字符串。不要害怕复制粘贴其他服务商和你自己的服务商。现在要添加新资源，我只需从我们的 droplet 复制，它就是我们的服务器资源提供者。在所有地方都做查找替换来改名字，然后再考虑逻辑问题，所以要大量复制粘贴。

Focus on composable and reusable functions, and then there's something called sweepers. This is like the "Oh shit" thing that runs afterwards to make sure that all of the resources are deleted, so you don't have stragglers hanging around. Some resources are a look at other providers. There are Terraform docs, guides, and source code. Again, read the source code. A couple videos. These are both two really good videos where they awalk through building a Terraform provider hands-on live. One of them is a little out of date, but the concepts are still there. The API changed a little bit, but watch these videos. If you're looking for someone to work on a provider or consulting company or you just want to pay someone to get it done, OpenCredo is someone that we worked with for a little bit. They kind of did some consulting education for us. So OpenCredo we highly recommend them as a dev shop to work on providers.
专注于可组合和可复用的函数，然后有一种叫做清道器的东西。这就像那个“糟了”的程序，之后会运行，确保所有资源都被删除，这样你就不会有落单的玩家在附近徘徊。有些资源可以介绍其他服务提供者。有Terraform的文档、指南和源代码。同样，请阅读源代码。看几个视频。这两段视频都非常精彩，他们亲自体验了如何现场打造Terraform服务提供商。其中一个有点过时了，但概念依然存在。API有点改动，但你可以看这些视频。如果你想找人帮某个供应商或咨询公司工作，或者只是想付钱请人帮你完成，OpenCredo 是我们合作过一段时间的合作伙伴。他们为我们做了一些咨询教育。所以我们强烈推荐OpenCredo作为开发团队来开发供应商。

With that, I am out of time. Right on the dot. You can find me on the internet @eddiezane. The link for the slides is at the bottom here, so if you want to grab the slides. Other than that, thank you all so much for listening, and hopefully this is helpful.
说到这里，我的时间到了。正好。你可以在网上找到我@eddiezane。幻灯片的链接在这里，如果你想拿幻灯片，可以直接下载。除此之外，非常感谢大家的倾听，希望这些对你有帮助。
